synthesis.body: A batched subprocess changes the blast radius of one bad input, and the batch API may return a PARTIAL result on failure. `git check-ignore --stdin -z` exits 128 for the whole invocation on a single unusable path — outside the repo, inside a nested git root, or carrying pathspec magic — while still echoing the candidates it processed before the failure. Discarding that output silently loses information; trusting it silently under-reports. Under the per-path loop it replaced, the damage from one bad input was one path. So when replacing N calls with one, decide explicitly what a non-success exit means for the whole batch, and treat a partial answer as unusable rather than as data. Preserving the loop as a documented fallback for the failing input is usually cheaper than making the batch total. The same reasoning applies to any fan-in rewrite, not just git. See ADR-0087.

title: Batching N subprocess calls into one changes the blast radius, and the batch may return a partial result
